name: date-field
pattern: A headless date field adding cancelable change events and state outputs to native input[type=date]
responsibility: Preserves native date value, min, max, step, segment editing, picker UI, and form semantics. Adds user-originated change events, data-state, and semantic markup validation that native input lacks. Does not generate appearance or content.

authorMarkup.label: The consumer provides an accessible name through <label>, aria-label, or aria-labelledby.
authorMarkup.range: The consumer supplies min, max, step, and value as native attributes.
authorMarkup.form: The consumer supplies name and uses native date-input form submission.
authorMarkup.content: The controller does not generate elements or content.

semanticElements: The root must be an HTMLInputElement with type=date.
contractValidation.invalidMarkup: Validate the root on connection. Invalid markup prevents listener registration, state output, and value operations and issues console.warn once per connection. Do not throw.
contractValidation.warning: Use the standard English disabling warning, including the required native input[type=date] root.

value.description: Current native input.value in YYYY-MM-DD format, or an empty string for missing/invalid input. Assignment changes value and data-state without custom events.

date-field:beforechange.when: Before a value change from trusted pointer or keyboard interaction (native change from segment editing or picker UI)

detail.value: The proposed value (YYYY-MM-DD or an empty string)

date-field:beforechange.effect: On preventDefault(), restore the previous native value and data-state and suppress date-field:change.

date-field:change.when: After a trusted value change is committed

events.programmatic: The value setter, initialization, form reset, and reconnection do not emit custom events.
events.sameValue: Do not emit beforechange/change when the value has not changed.
events.synthetic: input/change with isTrusted=false only synchronize native value and state outputs; they do not emit custom events. The controller does not dispatch synthetic native input/change events.

consumerIntegration.stimulusActions: Listen for date-field:change and date-field:beforechange on the root or an ancestor. The controller does not stop propagation.
consumerIntegration.cancelableHook: Cancel a change by calling event.preventDefault() in a date-field:beforechange listener.
consumerIntegration.programmatic: Other controllers may read/write value through a Stimulus controller reference or outlets. Programmatic API changes emit no events.
consumerIntegration.nested: Use :self or event.target === event.currentTarget to restrict events to the root when listening outside nested date-field controllers.

behavior.scope: Use one native input[type=date] as the root; there are no targets.
behavior.initial: Use the native value attribute as the initial value. The controller has no separate initial value.
behavior.native: Delegate segment navigation, increment/decrement, digit entry, deletion, picker UI, and form semantics to the browser. The controller neither validates nor corrects values.
behavior.disabled: Do not add data-* attributes for disabled state. Public API changes are allowed regardless of disabled state.

keyboard.native: Do not implement keyboard handling. All three engines provide native segment editing; the controller adds no keyboard operations.
keyboard.pageKeys: Do not implement PageUp/PageDown. Firefox handles them per segment (three months or seven days), while Chromium and WebKit do not respond; see docs/notes/browser-engine-differences.md. Whole-value day navigation would overlap Firefox segment editing and produce inconsistent results. The controller cannot determine segment focus, so it does not normalize this engine difference.

managedMarkup.nativeSemantics: Use native input[type=date] value, min, max, step, keyboard handling, and form semantics. There is no implicit role (MDN), and accessibility-tree exposure is engine-dependent.
managedMarkup.aria: Do not write role or aria-* attributes. Do not overwrite or remove authored ARIA.
managedMarkup.stateOnly: Only root data-state is a controller-managed state output. Do not output CSS custom properties.
managedMarkup.preservation: Preserve authored id, name, value, min, max, step, disabled, ARIA, and other attributes.

stateOutputs.ownership: Only root data-state is controller-owned; do not use ARIA as a visual state output.
stateOutputs.min: data-state="min" when value equals min. This state cannot occur without min.
stateOutputs.max: data-state="max" when value equals max. This state cannot occur without max.
stateOutputs.between: data-state="between" otherwise, including when value is empty.

lifecycle: Register root keydown, pointerdown, input, and change listeners and the associated-form reset listener in connect(); remove them in disconnect().
Synchronize state output from the current native value on reconnection.
Do not duplicate listeners or custom events when reconnecting the same instance.

observations.environment: Native browser pickers and screen readers on real devices
observations.item: Picker opening/closing, accessibility-tree exposure, and announcements
observations.impact: The controller retains native date input semantics and does not implement the picker or an alternative AT mapping.

acceptanceCriteria: Required AAA criteria: 2.1.3 Keyboard (No Exception), with no pointer-only features; and 3.2.5 Change on Request, with controller focus movement limited to user actions or consumer JS calls, never timers.
The behavior and accessibility implemented by this component must meet WCAG 2.2 Level AA.
Conforming input[type=date] preserves native value, min, max, step, segment editing, and form semantics; the controller does not intercept keyboard operations.
Only trusted value changes emit one cancelable beforechange followed by one committed change, in that order. Cancellation preserves value and state.
Public API calls, initialization, form reset, and reconnection synchronize state outputs without custom events.
The controller adds neither role nor aria-* attributes and preserves authored attributes.
Invalid markup disables enhancement with one warning
Pass automated tests in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit. Tests must not depend on WebKit delaying change until blur; see docs/notes/browser-engine-differences.md.
Report picker opening/closing, accessibility-tree exposure, and real-device screen reader announcements as unverified.

testMatrix.description: Synchronize character count after the trusted reset button's default action.
Synchronize checkbox-group/table-select master state after the trusted reset button's default action.
Preserve editable/password-field state when a later listener cancels reset.
Start editable viewing with the value after native reset.
Output the image-cropper initial snapshot to controls after native reset.
data-state min/max/between, missing min/max, empty values, and authored-attribute preservation
beforechange cancellation and restoration; change detail, order, and bubbling
Trusted native change from segment editing and its reason
No events from value assignment or synthetic input/change, with state synchronization
One warning and disabled enhancement for invalid roots

testMatrix: No controller handling of PageUp/PageDown (covered by date-field-native-change)
Engine-specific results for Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit
Screen-reader results on a real device (unverified)
